items.title: Govt. amends GO 97; polytechnic education to remain with TGCHE

items.title: After E20 Petrol, Indian Pumps Quietly Blending 5% Biodiesel In Diesel!
points: Diesel being sold at some fuel stations in India is now being blended with biodiesel at levels of up to 5%, according to industry information.
The blending is currently concentrated in areas where biodiesel is available, including parts of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Delhi-NCR.
Industry estimates cited in the report put biodiesel at around Rs 88 per litre, against roughly Rs 95.20 per litre for conventional diesel in Delhi-NCR.
Rating agency ICRA had estimated under-recoveries of about Rs 9 per litre on diesel in late September.
India's National Policy on Biofuels has an indicative target of 5% biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030.
The earlier IS 1460:2017 standard explicitly allowed up to 7% biodiesel in automotive diesel, while the current specification continues to regulate FAME content.
At most outlets, however, actual biodiesel blending is still far below 5%.
The Biodiesel Association of India says blends of up to 5% do not require a separate disclosure by oil companies under the automotive diesel standard.

items.title: US went easy on Pakistan’s military for years, says Blinken at HT Leadership Summit
points: Former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken on Saturday said Washington’s need for Pakistan’s help in Afghanistan had probably made it less critical of the military’s grip on Pakistan’s government.
He said the US no longer views India through a Pakistan lens.
“Seeing the relationship with India in some fashion through the prism of Pakistan, that is over and done,” Blinken said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit.
He said the earlier approach was driven by expedience, mainly the US’s goals in Afghanistan, and that this had ended, allowing Washington to recalibrate.
He drew a sharp line between the two relationships.
“These are fundamentally different relationships,” he said.
“There is an opportunity for the United States to do more to try to see that balance change.” But he said the US could not impose an outcome.
He described Pakistan as “a shadow” on India-US ties, and raised two concerns: the role of the Pakistani military in terrorism, and how civil-military imbalance undermines democracy in Pakistan.

items.title: India-US ties ‘essential’ to this century, but Washington must not expect India to follow it: Former Secretary of State Antony Blinken at HTLS
points: Former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken on Saturday called the India-US partnership an essential part of the new century.
He said Washington should not expect New Delhi to follow its lead, and that the US understood India’s long ties with Russia.
“I remain absolutely convinced that the relationship, partnership and strategic convergence between the United States and India are essential elements of this new century.
It is a relationship that we must continue to pursue and deepen,” Blinken said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit.
He was in conversation with Ambassador Javed Ashraf, chairman of the India Trade Promotion Organisation.
Blinken said the two countries had been “estranged democracies for 50 years”.
That changed over the next 25 years, starting towards the end of the Clinton administration and continuing under both Republican and Democratic presidents.
He called it “very hypocritical” for the US to press India on Russia now, when Washington has itself waived sanctions on Russia.

items.title: Microsoft shares defy massive global outage, close higher on Friday; Outlook, Teams services recover - Things to know
points: Microsoft shares showed resilience on Wall Street, recovering from an early pre-market decline to end marginally higher on Friday, even as the technology giant grappled with one of the longest global service disruptions in its history.
The outage, which affected workplace communications across more than 70 countries for over 24 hours, initially triggered investor concerns but failed to sustain pressure on the stock.
Microsoft shares had fallen around 2.5% to 3% in pre-market trading as the disruption entered its second day and uncertainty grew over when services would return to normal.
However, the stock recovered during the session and closed nearly flat, up 0.17% at $523.88.
The shares have gained roughly 8% so far this year.

The recovery came as Microsoft rolled out measures to stabilise its systems before confirming on Saturday, November 14, that services had been fully restored across Outlook, Teams, Copilot and the broader Microsoft 365 suite.
